text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright laid the foundation stone on Saturday for a new American general consulate in Ho Chi Minh City, which she said could become one of the busiest in the world.

-- Prosecutors have asked the three judges hearing appeals by 19 of the 22 convicted members of the Vu Xuan Truong drug syndicate not to show any mercy. Eight of the 19 were sentenced to death in the lower court.

-- Tuong Tan Sang, Secretary of the Communist Party Unit in Ho Chi Minh City, has rejected comments that the city's slow economic growth is a consequence of recent notorious financial scandals such as those surrounding Tamexco, EPCO and Minh Phung.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's People's Committee has temporarily halted the establishment of taxi businesses in the city.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam arrived in Hong Kong on Sunday to witness the handover of Hongkong to China.

-- Hanoi's leaders sent congratulations to China underlining that Vietnam always pays a lot of attention to strengthening and expanding the neighbourly relationship and multi-faceted cooperation with Chinese people on the mainland and in Hong Kong.
-- Foreign-invested projects licensed before November 23, 1996 can enjoy import tax exemption on construction material.

-- 211 foreign direct investment (FDI) projects with registered capital of $2.15 billion were approved in the first six months of 1997, bringing the total FDI projects in Vietnam to 1,729 with investment of $27.89 billion.
-- The Interior Ministry is planning an intensive programme to ensure traffic security before, during and after elections to the National Assembly on July 20.
-- A card-operated public telephone network will be installed nationwide, with some 4,600 telephone boxes being installed in two phases.
